title: Job Failure - Claims MMS job
description: Standard remediation for the Claims MMS job. This job is diagnosed entirely from S3, not CloudWatch: its most recent run log (in the error bucket) records the step number it failed at, and the keyword bucket's error/ folder may hold pending data files. Classifies the failure from BOTH facts before acting - only an early-stage failure (below step 5000) is safe to auto-remediate; anything at or past step 5000 always needs human review.
match_rule: Extract the failed step number from the phrase 'Failed at step <N>' (or an equivalent phrasing) in the most recent log file in the error bucket (eam-mmso-error-bucket-2330). Also check whether the keyword bucket's (eam-mmso-keyword-bucket-2330) error/ folder currently contains one or more files. Combine both facts per the decision tree below - this is a deterministic combination of two observed facts, not an independent root-cause diagnosis.

example_log_events.description: Real error-bucket log file content - step 4000 failure with a pending keyword file (matches the auto-retry rule)
example_log_events.raw_event:
JOB: Claims MMS job
START: 2026-07-08T22:10:00Z
STEP 3000: OK
STEP 3500: OK
ERROR: Failed at step 4000
Reason: Unable to process keyword file 'enrollment_batch_0417.dat' - validation error.
END: 2026-07-08T22:14:12Z
example_log_events.why: Step 4000 is below the 5000 threshold, and the keyword bucket's error/ folder contains the file that failed to process - safe to move it back to input/ so the job reprocesses it on its next run.

decision_tree.name: Classify the Claims MMS job failure by step number and pending keyword files
decision_tree.instruction: Read the failed step number from the most recent log file in the error bucket (e.g. 'Failed at step 4000'). Check whether the keyword bucket's error/ folder contains any files. Apply the matching condition below.

conditions.if: failed step is BELOW 5000 (step < 5000) AND one or more files exist in the keyword bucket's error/ folder
conditions.note: Early-stage failure with pending keyword files - safe to move them back to input/ so the job reprocesses them on its next scheduled run.

conditions.if: failed step is BELOW 5000 (step < 5000) AND the keyword bucket's error/ folder is empty
conditions.note: Early-stage failure but nothing pending in error/ - no remediation needed.

conditions.if: failed step is 5000 OR ABOVE (step >= 5000), regardless of whether files exist in error/
conditions.note: Late-stage failure - always needs human review regardless of pending keyword files, since a failure this far into the job is more likely to indicate a deeper issue than a simple, safely-retryable blip.

decision_tree.name: Verify remediation outcome
decision_tree.instruction: After move_keyword_files_to_input runs, confirm the moved files no longer appear in error/ and the job's next scheduled run reaches SUCCEEDED. If the job fails again, do not move files back a second time automatically.

conditions.note: Repeated failure - escalate rather than retry indefinitely.

feedback_notes: The failed step number and error-folder file presence are extracted deterministically from S3 content, not guessed. Auto-remediation (moving keyword files back to input/) is only applied for early-stage failures (below step 5000) per company policy; any failure at or past step 5000 always requires human review regardless of pending file state, since late failures are more likely to indicate a systemic issue than a simple transient blip that a file re-move would fix.
